facts.function: Bony framework of the posterior abdominal wall; attachment sites for psoas, iliacus and quadratus lumborum
Five large weight-bearing vertebrae; bodies and transverse processes anchor psoas major and quadratus lumborum
facts.attachments: Articulate with T12 above and sacrum below via intervertebral discs and zygapophysial (facet) joints

facts.function: Floating rib forming the superior boundary of the posterior abdominal wall
facts.attachments: Articulates with T12 body only; inferior border receives quadratus lumborum

subs.name: Iliac crest and iliac fossa (hip bone)

facts.function: Iliac crest anchors quadratus lumborum and abdominal wall muscles; iliac fossa gives origin to iliacus
facts.attachments: Iliac crest = superior border of ilium; iliac fossa = concave internal surface of ilium

facts.function: Common insertion of iliopsoas (psoas major + iliacus)
facts.attachments: Posteromedial projection at the junction of femoral neck and shaft

facts.function: Iliopsoas: chief flexor of the hip; flexes trunk when femur fixed
facts.attachments: Lumbar vertebrae and iliac fossa → lesser trochanter of femur

facts.function: Flexes hip; bilaterally flexes trunk, unilaterally laterally flexes lumbar spine
facts.attachments: Bodies, discs and transverse processes of T12–L5 → lesser trochanter of femur

facts.function: Flexes hip together with psoas major (iliopsoas)
facts.attachments: Iliac fossa, iliac crest, sacral ala → lesser trochanter via psoas tendon

facts.function: Extends and laterally flexes lumbar spine; fixes 12th rib during inspiration
facts.attachments: Iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament → 12th rib and transverse processes of L1–L4

facts.function: Elevates, retracts and upwardly rotates scapula; descending fibers elevate, ascending fibers depress
facts.innervation: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI); C3–C4 proprioception
facts.attachments: External occipital protuberance, nuchal ligament, C7–T12 spinous processes → lateral clavicle, acromion, scapular spine

facts.function: Extends, adducts and medially rotates the humerus
facts.attachments: T7–T12 spinous processes, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lower ribs → floor of intertubercular sulcus of humerus

facts.function: Elevates scapula and rotates glenoid inferiorly
facts.innervation: Dorsal scapular nerve (C5) and cervical nerves C3–C4
facts.attachments: Transverse processes of C1–C4 → medial border of scapula above the spine (superior angle)

facts.function: Retracts scapula, rotates glenoid inferiorly, fixes scapula to thoracic wall
facts.attachments: Spinous processes T2–T5 → medial border of scapula below the spine

facts.function: Retracts scapula, rotates glenoid inferiorly, fixes scapula to thoracic wall
facts.attachments: Nuchal ligament, spinous processes C7–T1 → medial border of scapula at root of spine

facts.function: Intermediate extrinsic back muscles; weak rib movers, likely mainly proprioceptive
Proposed to elevate upper ribs (inspiration); likely proprioceptive
facts.attachments: Nuchal ligament, spinous processes C7–T3 → superior borders of ribs 2–4

facts.function: Proposed to depress lower ribs (expiration); likely proprioceptive
facts.attachments: Spinous processes T11–L2 → inferior borders of ribs 8–12 near their angles

facts.function: Superficial intrinsic back layer; extend, laterally flex and ipsilaterally rotate head and neck
facts.innervation: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves

facts.function: Bilateral: extends head and neck; unilateral: laterally flexes and rotates face to same side
facts.innervation: Posterior rami of middle cervical spinal nerves
facts.attachments: Nuchal ligament, spinous processes C7–T3/T4 → mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line

facts.function: Bilateral: extends neck; unilateral: laterally flexes and rotates neck to same side
facts.innervation: Posterior rami of lower cervical spinal nerves
facts.attachments: Spinous processes T3–T6 → transverse processes of C1–C3/C4

facts.function: Chief extensors of the vertebral column; unilaterally laterally flex it
facts.attachments: Common tendon from posterior iliac crest, sacrum, lumbar spinous processes → ribs, vertebrae, skull

facts.function: Lateral column; extends and laterally flexes the vertebral column
facts.attachments: Common erector spinae tendon → angles of lower ribs and cervical transverse processes

facts.function: Intermediate column; extends vertebral column; capitis part extends head and turns face ipsilaterally
facts.attachments: Common tendon → thoracic and cervical transverse processes, ribs, mastoid process (capitis)

facts.function: Medial column; extends vertebral column
facts.attachments: Spinous processes of upper lumbar/lower thoracic vertebrae → spinous processes of upper thoracic vertebrae (and skull)

facts.function: Deep intrinsic group (semispinalis, multifidus, rotatores); stabilize, extend and contralaterally rotate vertebral column
facts.attachments: Transverse processes → spinous processes of more superior vertebrae

facts.function: Extends head and thoracic/cervical spine; rotates contralaterally
facts.attachments: Transverse processes C4–T10 → spinous processes 4–6 levels higher; capitis → occipital bone between nuchal lines

facts.function: Stabilizes vertebrae during local movement; thickest in lumbar region
facts.attachments: Sacrum, ilium, thoracic transverse and cervical articular processes → spinous processes 2–4 segments higher

facts.function: Contains vertebral artery (3rd part) and suboccipital nerve (C1 posterior ramus)
facts.attachments: Bounded by rectus capitis posterior major, obliquus capitis superior and inferior; floor = posterior atlanto-occipital membrane, C1 arch

facts.function: Unilateral: laterally flexes neck, turns face to opposite side; bilateral: flexes neck
facts.innervation: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI); C2–C3 proprioception
facts.attachments: Manubrium (sternal head) and medial clavicle (clavicular head) → mastoid process and lateral superior nuchal line

facts.function: Contains mastoid air cells continuous with the middle ear
facts.attachments: Insertion of SCM, splenius capitis, longissimus capitis; digastric posterior belly attaches at mastoid notch

facts.function: Contains spinal accessory nerve, cervical plexus branches, brachial plexus trunks, subclavian artery (3rd part), external jugular vein
facts.attachments: Bounded by posterior SCM, anterior trapezius border, middle third of clavicle; roof = investing fascia

facts.function: Superior part of sternum; jugular notch palpable in midline; origin of SCM sternal head
facts.attachments: Articulates with clavicles, 1st costal cartilages, and sternal body at sternal angle (T4/T5)

facts.function: Strut holding upper limb away from trunk; transmits limb forces to axial skeleton; often fractured at middle third
facts.attachments: Sternoclavicular joint medially, acromioclavicular joint laterally; SCM, trapezius, deltoid, pectoralis major attach

facts.function: Body bears weight; arch and body enclose vertebral foramen protecting spinal cord
facts.attachments: Arch = paired pedicles + laminae; bodies joined by intervertebral discs

facts.function: Short stout bar joining arch to body; vertebral notches form intervertebral foramina
facts.attachments: Connects vertebral body to lamina, transverse and articular processes

facts.function: Flat plate forming posterior vertebral arch; removed in laminectomy
facts.attachments: Joins pedicle to spinous process; ligamenta flava connect adjacent laminae

facts.function: Opening bounded by body and arch of one vertebra; transmits spinal cord and meninges
Stacked vertebral foramina; contains spinal cord, meninges, CSF, epidural fat, internal vertebral venous plexus
Lever for intrinsic back muscles; palpable midline landmark
facts.attachments: Projects posteriorly from junction of laminae; supraspinous and interspinous ligaments attach

facts.function: Lever and attachment site for deep back muscles
facts.attachments: Projects laterally from pedicle–lamina junction; thoracic ones articulate with rib tubercles

facts.function: Transmits spinal nerve, dorsal root ganglion and segmental vessels
facts.attachments: Bounded by adjacent pedicle notches, disc and bodies anteriorly, facet joint posteriorly

facts.function: Seven vertebrae; small bodies, transverse foramina, bifid spinous processes (C3–C6)
facts.attachments: Uncovertebral joints between bodies; C7 = vertebra prominens

facts.function: Transmits vertebral artery (C6–C1) and vertebral veins; C7 usually transmits only veins
Supplies brainstem, cerebellum, posterior cerebrum and spinal cord (posterior circulation)
facts.attachments: Subclavian branch → transverse foramina C6–C1 → suboccipital triangle → foramen magnum → joins partner to form basilar

facts.function: Twelve rib-bearing vertebrae; heart-shaped bodies, long inferiorly sloping spinous processes
facts.attachments: Costal facets on bodies (rib heads) and on transverse processes (rib tubercles, T1–T10)

facts.function: Articular surfaces for the ribs
facts.attachments: Superior/inferior costal facets on body → rib heads; transverse costal facet → rib tubercle (T1–T10)

facts.function: Five largest vertebrae; kidney-shaped bodies, hatchet-shaped spinous processes
facts.attachments: Sagittally oriented facets limit rotation; mammillary processes anchor multifidus

facts.function: Flexion–extension of head (nodding, 'yes')
facts.attachments: Occipital condyles ↔ superior articular facets of atlas (C1); atlas lacks body and spinous process

facts.function: Rotation of head ('no'); about half of cervical rotation
facts.attachments: Dens of axis (C2) ↔ anterior arch of atlas, held by transverse ligament; plus paired lateral atlantoaxial joints

facts.function: Conducts ascending and descending tracts; cervical and lumbosacral enlargements supply limbs; 31 segment pairs
facts.attachments: Continuous with medulla at foramen magnum → ends as conus medullaris at L1–L2 in adults
facts.supply: One anterior and two posterior spinal arteries, reinforced by segmental medullary arteries (artery of Adamkiewicz)

facts.function: Tapered end of spinal cord at L1–L2 (adult); gives rise to filum terminale
facts.attachments: Filum terminale anchors cord to coccyx

facts.function: Lumbar, sacral and coccygeal roots descending in lumbar cistern below conus; compression → saddle anesthesia, bowel/bladder dysfunction
Carries afferent (sensory) fibers into dorsal horn
facts.attachments: Bears dorsal root ganglion (sensory cell bodies) in the intervertebral foramen

facts.function: Carries efferent motor fibers from anterior horn (plus preganglionic sympathetics at T1–L2)
Mixed (motor + sensory) nerve formed by union of dorsal and ventral roots; 31 pairs
facts.attachments: Exits intervertebral foramen → divides into anterior and posterior rami

facts.function: Supplies anterolateral trunk and limbs; forms cervical, brachial, lumbar, sacral plexuses and intercostal nerves
Supplies intrinsic (deep) back muscles, zygapophysial joints and overlying back skin
Tough outermost meninx; dural sac ends at S2
facts.attachments: Attached to foramen magnum margin; separated from vertebrae by epidural space; sleeves follow nerve roots

facts.function: Avascular middle meninx lining dura; encloses CSF in subarachnoid space
facts.attachments: Held against dura by CSF pressure; ends with dural sac at S2

facts.function: Innermost meninx adherent to cord; forms denticulate ligaments and filum terminale
facts.attachments: Denticulate ligaments anchor cord laterally to dura

facts.function: Between dura and vertebral canal walls; contains fat and internal vertebral venous plexus; site of epidural anesthesia
Potential space between dura and arachnoid; normally contains no CSF
Between arachnoid and pia; contains CSF and spinal vessels; site of spinal anesthesia
Enlarged subarachnoid space from conus (L2) to S2; contains cauda equina and CSF; lumbar puncture at L3–L4 or L4–L5
